title: About Me
exam_focus: Listening: form completion with names, spelling and numbers
Reading: True / False and sentence completion (ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER)
Writing: forms and a short personal profile
goals: spell names and places in English
say and write numbers 0–100 and phone numbers
complete a form with personal information
answer Speaking Part 1 questions about myself

sections.title: The alphabet and spelling
sections.goal: spell names and places, letter by letter

blocks.text: English letters are in **seven sound groups**. Say each group aloud.

head: Sound
Letters
rows: B C D E G P T V

blocks.title: Exam skill: spelling
items: In IELTS Listening, people often **spell names and places**. A wrong letter means a wrong answer.
Be careful with **A / E / I**, **G / J**, **B / P / V** and **M / N**.
**Double L** means LL: *Bella* = B-E-double L-A.

blocks.instruction: Which letter has a different sound? Write it.
Listen and write the names.

sections.title: Numbers and phone numbers
sections.goal: say and hear numbers, and tell 13 from 30

blocks.title: Exam skill: numbers
items: **13 or 30?** thir**TEEN** has the stress at the end; **THIR**ty has it at the start.
In phone numbers, **0** is often *oh*, and **55** is *double five*.
Spelling: forty (not *fourty*), nineteen, ninety.

blocks.instruction: Write the numbers in words.
Listen and choose the number you hear.
Listen again and write the phone numbers.

sections.title: Countries and personal information
sections.goal: talk about countries, nationalities and personal details

blocks.title: Nationality endings
items: **-an / -ian:** America → American, Russia → Russian, Egypt → Egyptian
**-ish:** the UK → British, Turkey → Turkish
**-ese:** Vietnam → Vietnamese
Countries, nationalities and languages always start with a **capital letter**.

blocks.instruction: Write the nationality.

items.ex: My date of birth is 5 May 2007.
I'm a student at a college.

items.q: Bukhara is my ______. I'm from there.

sections.title: be: am / is / are
sections.goal: use am / is / are in statements, negatives and questions

blocks.text: Use **be** to talk about your name, age, country, nationality and job.

blocks.title: a / an + job
items: I'm **a** student. She's **a** doctor.
He's **an** engineer. I'm **an** English teacher. (**an** before a, e, i, o, u sounds)

items.right: I am 19. / I am 19 years old.

blocks.instruction: Choose the correct word.

items.q: Aziz and Kamola (is / are) from Bukhara.
Our teacher (is / are) from South Korea.

blocks.instruction: Make the sentences negative. Use short forms.

items.a: She isn't a doctor. / She's not a doctor.
We aren't from Kazakhstan. / We're not from Kazakhstan.
They aren't Turkish. / They're not Turkish.

blocks.instruction: Put the words in order to make questions. Then ask and answer the questions with a partner.
blocks.example: from / you / are / where → **Where are you from?**

blocks.instruction: Correct the mistakes.
blocks.example: My sister doctor. → **My sister is a doctor.**

sections.title: IELTS Listening: form completion
sections.goal: complete a form while you listen

blocks.text: In IELTS Listening Part 1, you hear a conversation and complete a **form** or **notes**. The answers are often names, numbers and short words.

blocks.title: Exam skill: before you listen
items: Read the form. For each gap, decide: is it a **name**, a **number** or a **word**?
Listen for **corrections**: *It's 25… sorry, no, it's 52.* The second answer is correct.
Write **ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER**. Check your spelling.

blocks.instruction: Look at the form in the next exercise. What kind of answer is each gap? Write *name*, *number* or *word*.
Questions 1–6. Listen and complete the form. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.

blocks.instruction: Listen again. Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

sections.title: IELTS Reading: True / False and sentence completion
sections.goal: scan a text for names, numbers and key words

blocks.title: Exam skill: scanning
items: **Scan** the text: look quickly for names, numbers and key words from the question.
Then read that part slowly to find the answer.
In sentence completion, copy the word **from the text** and spell it correctly.

blocks.title: Meet our students
blocks.intro: Bright Star Language Centre, Tashkent · Student profiles

paras.head: Aziz
paras.text: Hello! I'm Aziz and I'm 22. I'm from Samarkand, but now I'm in Tashkent. I'm an engineer at a bus company. My English class is in the evening. Our teacher is Ms Lee. She's from South Korea and she's very friendly. Our class is small – we are eight students.

paras.head: Maria
paras.text: Hi, I'm Maria. I'm 30 and I'm Spanish. My hometown is Valencia, a big city in Spain. I'm a nurse at a hospital in Tashkent. My husband is Uzbek, so Uzbek is my second language! English is important for my job. My class is in the morning.

paras.head: Aigerim
paras.text: Hello, my name's Aigerim. I'm 17 and I'm Kazakh – my city is Almaty. I'm not a university student. I'm at school. I want to study at a university in the UK, so IELTS is very important for me. My English class is on Saturday. It's my favourite day!

blocks.instruction: Questions 1–5. Read the text. Write TRUE or FALSE.
Questions 6–9. Complete the sentences. Write ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER from the text.

items.q: There are ______ students in Aziz's class.
Maria is a nurse at a ______.

sections.title: IELTS Speaking Part 1
sections.goal: answer Part 1 questions with one extra detail

blocks.text: In **Speaking Part 1** (4–5 minutes), the examiner asks simple questions about you: your name, home, work or studies.

blocks.title: Model: Part 1
lines: Can you tell me your full name, please?
I'm from Bukhara. It's a beautiful old city.
Do you work or are you a student?
I'm a student. I'm at a college in Tashkent.
Is your hometown big or small?
It's quite big. It's famous for its old buildings.

blocks.title: Exam skill: the +1 rule
items: Don't answer with one word (*Bukhara.*). Give the answer **+1 more piece of information**.
*I'm from Bukhara.* **+** *It's a beautiful old city.*

blocks.instruction: Make the answers longer. Match the answers (1–5) with the extra information (A–E).
right: I'm at a school in Andijan.
It's a popular name in Uzbekistan.

blocks.instruction: Pronunciation: write the short forms. Then say them.
Work in pairs. Student A is the examiner. Ask the questions. Student B answers with the +1 rule. Then change roles.
items: What's your full name?
Can you spell your surname, please?
Where are you from?
Is your hometown big or small?
Do you work or are you a student?
What languages do you speak?

sections.title: Forms and a short profile
sections.goal: complete a form and write a short profile

blocks.title: Model: About me
blocks.text: Hello! My name is Kamola Tursunova. I'm 18 and I'm Uzbek. I'm from Termez, a city in the south of Uzbekistan. I'm a student at a college in Tashkent. My languages are Uzbek, Russian and a little English. English is important for me because IELTS is my goal.

blocks.title: Capital letters
items: Use a capital letter for **names** (Kamola), **cities** (Termez), **countries** (Uzbekistan), **nationalities and languages** (Uzbek, English), **I**, and the **first word** of a sentence.
In IELTS, a spelling mistake makes an answer wrong. Check every word.

blocks.instruction: Correct the capital letters.

items.q: my name is olga and i'm russian.
items.a: My name is Olga and I'm Russian.

items.q: ahmed is egyptian. he speaks arabic.
items.a: Ahmed is Egyptian. He speaks Arabic.

items.q: our teacher is from the usa.
items.a: Our teacher is from the USA.

scripts.title: Spelling names
scripts.notes: One speaker per item (mix male/female). Spell slowly, with a short pause between letters.
lines: Number one. My first name is Jasur. J-A-S-U-R.
Number two. Her name is Gulnora. G-U-L-N-O-R-A.
Number three. His surname is Valiyev. V-A-L-I-Y-E-V.
Number four. My name's Emily. E-M-I-L-Y.
Number five. Our teacher's surname is Yusupova. Y-U-S-U-P-O-V-A.

scripts.title: Numbers and phone numbers
scripts.notes: Clear stress: thirTEEN vs THIRty. Phone numbers grouped as written.
lines: Hi, it's Bekzod. My number is two-six-seven, double four, nine-one.
Hello, this is Anna. My phone number is oh-seven-five, double eight, three, oh, two.

scripts.title: Joining a language centre
scripts.notes: Receptionist (female, 30s) and Dilnoza (female, 19). Natural but slow. The address correction must be clear.
lines: Good morning, Bright Star Language Centre. How can I help you?
Hello. I'd like to join an English course, please.
Of course. I need some information for the form. What's your first name?
How do you spell that, please?
R-A-K-H-I-M-O-V-A. Thank you. And how old are you, Dilnoza?
Yes, I am. I'm a student at a medical college.
It's twenty-five Navoi Street… Oh, sorry, no. It's fifty-two. Fifty-two Navoi Street.
Fifty-two Navoi Street. Thanks. Now, is the morning a good time for your lessons?
No, I'm at college in the morning. The evening is good for me.
OK, the evening. Our evening classes are on Monday, Wednesday and Friday.
Great. I want to study English with you. Thank you very much.

scripts.title: A library card
scripts.notes: Librarian (female) and Timur (male, 20). The date correction must be clear: sixth → sixteenth.
lines: Hello. Do you want a library card?
And what's your date of birth?
The sixth of May… no, sorry, the sixteenth of May, two thousand and six.
The sixteenth of May. What's your nationality?
Four-seven-one, double nine, three-two. And are you a student?
No, I'm not. I'm a driver.
